text: Debugging is an important skill for every programmer. When a program does not work as expected, the first step is identifying bugs. You need to find where and why the error happens. Good debugging tools, such as breakpoints and step-by-step execution, can help you inspect your code closely. It is also wise to follow a systematic approach: reproduce the problem, form a hypothesis, test it, and repeat until you find the cause. Logging is another useful technique because it records what your program does while it runs. With clear logs, you can trace errors more easily. By combining these strategies, you can solve problems faster and become a more confident developer.
